intent: Three concepts only; no native implementation approved.

concepts.title: A · Destination trays
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity 16:9 landscape concept for the existing Legend of the Five Rings Emperor digital card game. The attached screenshot is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: preserve the warm timber fortress, navy cloth, black lacquer, thin patinated brass edging, cream Caudex-like serif text and weathered brush headings. Redesign the Top Cards interaction radically for clear drag and drop. Do not reproduce the confusing old buttons. No modern dashboard, white panels, web cards, giant bevels or extra ornaments. Full upright uncropped card faces with illustrations; tiny generated card text is illustrative. Keep main interaction labels unusually legible and sparse.
Scenario is exactly Banish All Doubt: look at four cards of YOUR Fate deck, take exactly ONE into your hand, put the other THREE on the BOTTOM in any order. All four faces are private. No discard, top-of-deck, reveal, opponent or other unavailable destination. Four unique card faces TOTAL, each rendered once, no duplicate thumbnails. Full card faces must remain unobscured. Show one card mid-drag and three remaining cards, with clear target outline and a restrained lifted shadow. Card movement, not dropdowns or per-card action buttons, is the main interaction. Footer contains just quiet Undo and a single final Confirm arrangement (muted while dragging); moving cards is a reversible draft. Do not invent game rules or values.
Direction A: a single spacious lacquer tray centered over the softly dimmed game table. Small eyebrow “A · DESTINATION TRAYS”. Main heading “BANISH ALL DOUBT”; one short line “Drag 1 card into your hand. Arrange the other 3 at the bottom.” Small privacy note “Only you can see these cards.”
The tray has TWO very clear large adjacent destinations and very little other chrome. LEFT 72%: three big full card faces side by side in a single return row, grouped under “BOTTOM OF YOUR FATE DECK”. A small low face-down remainder stack anchors the left edge of this row with label “Rest of deck”; it is spatially separate from the three faces. A very thin gold reading line travels from the remainder stack through the three slots. Labels immediately below the three faces: “1 · Below the deck”, “2”, “3 · Very bottom”. The first and last labels must be unmistakable. No top-deck label anywhere.
RIGHT 28%: one tall card-sized destination well headed “YOUR HAND” and “Choose 1”. A simple subtle fan-of-cards motif sits behind the empty slot. The FOURTH full card is lifted in transit toward that hand slot, not obscuring other cards, with an unobtrusive hand cursor. The hand destination has a clear ivory-gold border and a soft inset silhouette, not neon. Caption directly above the destination reads “Release to put in hand”. Keep the three remaining faces large at roughly 260–330 px height on a 1920-wide canvas. Large breathing room, one glance must explain what goes into hand and what stays at bottom. No extra repeated explanation, no steps, no side inspector, no buttons below individual cards.

Footer contains just quiet Undo and a single final Confirm arrangement (muted while dragging); moving cards is a reversible draft. Do not invent game rules or values.
Direction B: physically explicit DECK LADDER, a distinct vertical layout, not a horizontal sorting tray. Centered lacquer review surface over softly dimmed fortress table; small eyebrow “B · THE PHYSICAL DECK”; heading “BANISH ALL DOUBT”, short instruction “Keep 1. Place the rest beneath your deck.” Privacy “Only you can see these cards.”
LEFT/CENTER 65%: a compact physical face-down stack at the TOP labeled “REST OF YOUR FATE DECK”. A thin vertical brass spine goes downward from the bottom edge of that stack. THREE separate, full uncropped upright card faces are placed down the spine in three rows, all visible with ample gaps. These are face-up draft previews, not actual public cards. Each face height about 170 px on a 1080-high canvas, preserve full portrait aspect ratio, no overlap or fanning. Beside each card, a short label aligned to its row: “1 · Immediately below the deck”, “2 · Below card 1”, “3 · Very bottom”. Row 3 has a small horizontal end-cap at the base so the absolute deck bottom is visually clear. Avoid three nested boxes: use one continuous connected deck-order region. This is literally a readable top-to-bottom map of the resulting stack.
RIGHT 35%: generous destination region labeled “YOUR HAND · 1 CARD” with ONE card-sized target. A fourth full card is mid-drag toward it, lifted and slightly tilted with a small cursor, and the destination glows very subtly. “Release to keep” over the slot. Do not show any other card faces or unavailable zones. Visually connect ordering to the physical stack, not an abstract numbered table. Calm sparse typography, thin material frames. The vertical deck spine and the spatial relationship are the differentiating ideas, not decoration.

Direction C: DIRECT TABLE DROP ZONES, NO central modal or full-screen lacquer dialog. In the existing right sidebar show a compact task heading “BANISH ALL DOUBT”, “Your Fate deck”, and “Take 1 card. Return 3 to the bottom.” Small “Private view” label. Quiet Undo and single final Confirm arrangement live at bottom of this sidebar.
The three remaining large full card faces hover in a straight ordered row directly ABOVE the player's physical Fate deck on the navy table. This temporary row is clearly framed by a thin elegant brass bracket, with a single label “RETURN TO BOTTOM” above it. Beneath the row show “1 · Below the deck”, “2”, “3 · Very bottom”. A restrained brass leader joins this bracket to the LOWER EDGE of the visible face-down Fate stack, showing explicitly that they slide beneath it; avoid arrow buttons, confusion with the deck TOP, or long sweeping arrows. Three return faces are each about 260 px tall and fully visible; do not scatter them around the table.
At the lower edge of the board, where the player's existing hand lives, create ONE broad temporary empty highlighted insertion slot with a subtle card-fan icon and clear large text “YOUR HAND · DROP 1 CARD HERE”. The FOURTH viewed card is visibly lifted mid-drag down toward that hand insertion target, not duplicated in the source row, with a small cursor. Existing unrelated hand cards remain dimmed so no extra example faces confuse the four-card task. The spatial targets do the explaining. No per-card buttons, no dropdowns, no giant extra plaque, no crowded labels. Practical native game mockup, clean and legible, visibly different from the other overlay concepts.
